history.hypothesis: The failure is caused by state leaking across executions in the nested PrimitiveBytes class, so running the test repeatedly in one JVM will expose stale static values or iteration counts that a fresh-JVM rerun cannot detect.

diagnosis.root_cause: PrimitiveBytes.iterations and PrimitiveBytes.values are static mutable state that is never reset between executions of primitiveBytes. T2 executes the test twice in the same JVM, so the second execution observes iterations equal to 200 instead of the expected default trial count of 100, causing the assertion at line 119 to fail.

evidence.why: The test expects PrimitiveBytes.iterations to equal one trial count on every execution, but it does not reset the static counter before calling testResult.
Both iterations and values are static and persist across test executions; each property invocation appends to values and increments iterations, so a second execution doubles the accumulated count.
The reproduced failure is AssertionError expected 100 but was 200 at this assertion, directly confirming accumulation from the first same-JVM execution.

history.hypothesis: The test leaks the static BoxOfFoo.iterations counter between executions, so running it twice in the same JVM will make the second assertion observe more than the default trial count.

diagnosis.root_cause: The nested BoxOfFoo test class stores its trial count in the static field iterations, but the field is never reset between executions. Each testResult(BoxOfFoo.class) invocation runs the property for the default 100 trials and increments the same static counter, so the second execution observes 200 instead of 100.

evidence.why: The assertion compares the expected default trial count with a static counter after executing BoxOfFoo. Repeating the outer test in the same JVM reuses the counter rather than starting from zero; the failure stack identifies this assertion at line 45.

iterations is static and holds() increments it once per generated trial. It is not reset after a run, so the first 100-trial execution leaves 100 in the field and the second execution increments it to 200.

history.hypothesis: The test leaks static iterations and values across executions, so running it twice in the same JVM will make the second assertion inspect stale accumulated state and fail.

diagnosis.root_cause: The nested WrapperChars property stores execution state in static fields that are never reset. When the test is executed a second time in the same JVM, WrapperChars.iterations continues from 100 and reaches 200, while wrapperChars still expects the default trial count of 100.

evidence.why: The failing assertion at line 185 always expects the static iteration counter to equal the default trial count, including on repeated executions.

WrapperChars.iterations and WrapperChars.values are static state, and each property trial increments iterations without clearing it between test executions. The reproduced second subrun therefore observes 200 iterations instead of 100.
